facts.statement: Chenanisuchus was discovered by expeditions in 2000 and formally described in 2005.
facts.quote: It was described in 2005, after expeditions uncovered it in 2000.

facts.statement: Fossils found in Mali indicate that Chenanisuchus survived the Cretaceous-Paleogene extinction event.
facts.quote: Fossils of Chenanisuchus were also found in Maastrichtian age strata in Mali, showing that Chenanisuchus survived the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.

facts.statement: Based on a 60-centimeter skull, the adult animal is estimated to have reached 4 to 4.5 meters in length.
facts.quote: Chenanisuchus lateroculi has an estimated adult length between 4 and 4.5 meters, based on the 60 centimeter long skull.

facts.statement: Among dyrosaurids, Chenanisuchus possesses the shortest snout relative to skull length, though it is thicker and less slender than in species like Sokotosuchus.
facts.quote: It has the shortest snout relative to the dorsal skull length among all dyrosaurids, but its snout is thicker and its skull less slender than in dyrosaurids such as Sokotosuchus.

facts.statement: It is suggested that their ability to walk on the sea floor helped dyrosaurids like Chenanisuchus survive the K-Pg extinction.
facts.quote: This mode of subaqueous locomotion is suggested to have contributed to the survival of dyrosaurids such as Chenanisuchus across the K-Pg boundary.

facts.statement: Chenanisuchus belongs to the family Dyrosauridae.
